rows.text: The Gemma B70 decode benchmark evaluates autoregressive throughput under varying KV cache constraints. To establish a reliable benchmark, the test utilizes a fixed prompt length to isolate decoding latency. This benchmark measures tokens per second (TPS) across multiple GPU configurations. A critical benchmark metric is the memory bandwidth utilization during the decoding phase. In this benchmark, the B70 architecture demonstrates high efficiency in compute-bound scenarios. However, the benchmark reveals that memory-bound bottlenecks emerge as sequence length increases. To refine the benchmark, we must account for batch size scaling. Each benchmark iteration ensures consistent precision settings to maintain benchmark validity. The benchmark results indicate that Gemma B70 optimizes the attention mechanism for this specific benchmark. Consequently, the benchmark serves as a standard for comparing large-scale decoder performance. Final benchmark analysis suggests that hardware interconnect speed heavily influences the benchmark outcome.
